articles.title: Zoom into a camera’s live view
articles.dek: Consistent playback controls replace browser-specific ones, and the viewing window keeps the screen awake.
body: A wide camera view can hide the detail you want to check. Home Assistant’s camera detail dialog lets you enlarge the picture with a pinch, double-click or Ctrl/Cmd-scroll, then drag around it. A small overview shows your position, with a button to reset the view.

Wendelin replaces the browser’s video controls with a consistent set for sound, full screen and picture-in-picture. Cameras that supply a sequence of still images gain picture-in-picture when those frames can be copied; streams from another origin cannot use it. Android’s separate player for HEVC, a video compression format, remains outside the new controls and zoom.

The related public camera-interface proposal advances from Shaping to Building. Matthias Kerstner refined its scope with Abílio Costa, who distinguished enlarging the image on screen from moving the physical camera or changing its lens. That scope guides this work; the roadmap gives no release date.

pullRequests.title: Add a camera player with its own controls to the more info

externalSources.title: Refine the camera UI and introduce card zooming

articles.title: Let an automation look back at what happened
articles.dek: A new action retrieves recorded state changes, including entities that have no long-term statistics.
body: A vacuum routine can check how often cleaning ran during the past week before deciding to start again. Home Assistant adds recorder.get_history, making the stored sequence of entity states available inside automations and scripts instead of requiring an external history request.

The result gives each state a start and end time within the requested period. It excludes attributes and repeated records whose state did not change. Queries remain limited by what the recorder retains and by the record limit per entity; they do not recover history that has already been removed.

pullRequests.title: Add `recorder.get_history` action
Document recorder.get_history action

articles.title: New SmartThings connections need a personal token
articles.dek: Existing cloud-login entries move to the revised setup when they next need authentication.
body: Adding SmartThings changes from a Home Assistant Cloud sign-in to credentials for your own SmartThings app. The integration asks for a Personal Access Token with the application permissions selected, from an account with an active SmartThings API plan, then creates or reuses the app for that Home Assistant instance.

Existing entries that use the cloud login follow this route when they next reauthenticate. If the account lacks the required entitlement or exceeds its API quota, the integration reports that specific problem and points to plan management instead of hiding it behind a generic failed command.

pullRequests.title: Use PAT based app provisioning in SmartThings

articles.title: Manage spoken timers from a dashboard
articles.dek: ESPHome satellites expose the same timers to automations; reloading the integration clears active and paused timers.
body: A timer started through an ESPHome voice satellite no longer has to be managed only by speaking to it. Home Assistant exposes supported satellites’ timers as timer-list entities, connecting the same running timers to dashboards, automations and voice commands without changing the firmware protocol.

The change also affects reloads: active and paused timers belong to the timer-list entity and are cleared when the ESPHome integration reloads. Avoid reloading while they are needed, or recreate them afterwards. Timers remain in memory and are also lost on a restart.

pullRequests.title: Add timer lists to ESPHome voice satellites

articles.title: Find speakers across the server’s local networks
articles.dek: Virtual connections stay out of the default search; players on a Docker bridge need an explicit setting.
body: A music server connected to two local networks can find players on both without a special discovery setting. Music Assistant’s default search includes all local network connections except virtual ones, instead of using only the connection carrying its default route.

Docker, virtual-machine, VPN and Thread connections stay outside that default. This also changes Linux hosts using IPv6, the newer internet addressing system, which previously searched every connection. Players on a Docker bridge on the same host need the “All interfaces” setting; the ordinary option is named “Local network interfaces”.
This uses the networks the server is already connected to. It does not make discovery cross a router into networks the server cannot reach.

pullRequests.title: Discover players on every local network the server is connected to

articles.title: Saving device settings stops causing repeated restarts
articles.dek: The correction targets ESP8266 boards that write values to flash while Wi-Fi is busy.
body: A sensor or controller that frequently saves its state to permanent memory could restart during Wi-Fi traffic. ESPHome keeps network processing running while writing those values, preventing the memory shortage that caused the crash. The affected ESP8266 configurations enable restore_from_flash or explicitly save preferences to flash.

In J. Nick Koston’s roughly hour-long NodeMCU comparison, settings were saved every second while the board scanned for networks and received frequent pings. The earlier build restarted fourteen times; the corrected build completed 3,096 saves without a reset.

pullRequests.title: [esp8266] Keep interrupts enabled while saving preferences to flash

articles.title: See the cost beside your electricity use
articles.dek: The selected period includes export credits and uses the prices or cost sensors you have configured.
body: Electricity sent back to the grid can offset what you buy during the same day or month. Home Assistant’s Energy dashboard puts that net amount in the Electricity Usage card, subtracting export compensation from the cost of imported power.

The amount follows the selected period and the configured cost statistics or fixed rates, formatted in the local currency. It can show a credit for net exporters; it stays hidden when no prices or cost sensors are configured.

pullRequests.title: Add dynamic period cost indicator chip to Energy Usage Graph

media.caption: The Electricity Usage graph shows a monetary total alongside the selected period’s energy use.

articles.title: A quiet voice satellite spends less time listening for “stop”
articles.dek: A Pi Zero W test measures lower idle processor use; recognition has a short warm-up when it resumes.
body: A stop command matters while a voice assistant is speaking, not throughout the silence between requests. Linux Voice Assistant pauses that detector when it is not needed, reducing the continuous work on small computers.

On a Raspberry Pi Zero W Rev 1.1, @Joldiges measured the process using 41.9% of its single core before the change and 30.9% afterward, in 480-second idle samples with other services running. A second 300-second sample measured 32.8%. Music playback was not active during these tests, and this does not establish full support for that older board.

A related change pauses wake-word detection during a conversation and keeps each word tied to its own sensitivity setting. The detectors need a short warm-up when they resume: a wake word spoken in roughly the first 0.2 seconds after a conversation can be missed.

pullRequests.title: Gate idle stop-word inference behind active_wake_words
Pause wake word detection during a pipeline and extract it into its own module

articles.title: One homemade proxy can accept different Z-Wave USB adapters
articles.dek: Only one radio is active at a time; unplugging it allows another configured adapter to take over.
body: A homemade box that connects a USB radio to the network no longer needs separate firmware for each supported adapter driver. ESPHome accepts a list of USB serial connections and uses the first connected one, keeping it until it is unplugged.

Keith Burzinski tested an Ethernet-connected ESP32-S3 with a Home Assistant Connect ZWA-2 and a Zooz ZST39 LR. Switching adapters clears the previous network identifier and reads the replacement’s own identifier; it does not transfer a Z-Wave network between radios. Traffic received by an inactive adapter is discarded before it becomes active.

pullRequests.title: [zwave_proxy] Accept several UARTs and use the first one that is connected
[uart] Find a UART named in a list of ids when checking exclusive use

articles.title: Sleeping Bluesound speakers return without another restart
articles.dek: A stereo pair’s empty preset list also stops blocking other players during setup.
body: A NAD or Bluesound player that takes too long to answer when Music Assistant starts remains in the player list as unavailable, then returns through regular polling once it responds. Previously, the failed first response could prevent it from being added at all.

A second correction treats an unreadable preset list as empty. Some secondary speakers in BluOS stereo pairs return an empty reply; that no longer stops setup for the pair and every player discovered afterward. The startup recovery was verified with a NAD C658; the stereo-pair case has automated coverage rather than a hardware test.

pullRequests.title: Add a Bluesound player that doesn't answer at startup as unavailable
Keep adding Bluesound players when a stereo pair speaker has no presets

articles.title: Check whether a console received its new play limit
articles.dek: The timestamp comes from Nintendo’s settings sync, not Home Assistant’s last poll.
body: After changing a bedtime, play limit or bonus time, a new Last synced sensor shows when the console last received parental-control settings from Nintendo. Each console gets its own timestamp in Home Assistant; it is unknown when Nintendo supplies no sync time.
The console only synchronizes while online. This distinguishes a setting you requested from the last time the device checked in with Nintendo.

pullRequests.title: Add last synced sensor to Nintendo Parental Controls

articles.title: Kaadas locks stop rejecting valid numeric PINs
articles.dek: A compatibility correction covers the KA211 and KA200, whose reported key capabilities were misread.
body: Entering a code such as 1234 could fail before Z-Wave JS sent anything to the lock. The affected devices described their numeric keys incorrectly, making every ordinary digit look unsupported. Device-specific settings supply the intended digits instead.

The correction covers the KA211 and KA200. The reported failure came from a US KA211; the KA200 uses matching capabilities and firmware in its certification, with automated tests covering both device identities.

pullRequests.title: fix(config): override User Code capabilities for Kaadas locks 0x00c7 and 0x00c8

articles.title: A detached Shelly wall switch can trigger automations
articles.dek: The Wave 1PM keeps its relay separate while forwarding both switch positions.
body: A physical toggle could send commands to the controller without Home Assistant receiving a usable input event. Z-Wave JS maps those commands to events for the Shelly Wave 1PM, making the detached input useful without changing the relay output.

@realstoff makes a first contribution to Z-Wave JS after testing both positions on a Wave 1PM in toggle-switch mode. The controller must be assigned to association group 2, the device’s destination for these switch commands.

pullRequests.title: fix(config): expose Shelly Wave 1PM Basic Set as events

articles.title: Radiator valves regain finer heating control
articles.dek: Sonoff TRVZB firmware 1.4.9 enters Zigpy’s update catalog with corrections for Adaptive Mode.
body: A valve could turn the heat on or off outside its configured temperature tolerance. The release notes for Sonoff TRVZB firmware 1.4.9 describe a correction, alongside a fix for Adaptive Mode alternating only between fully open and fully closed.
The image joins Zigpy’s update catalog and is marked as tested on a device. Applying that firmware is a separate step; the catalog entry does not update every installation automatically.

pullRequests.title: Add Sonoff TRVZB v1.4.9

articles.title: A second chance to find lyrics that follow the song
articles.dek: An existing library entry may wait for its next metadata refresh before receiving the improvement.
body: A song supplied with ordinary lyrics by Deezer or Bandcamp can still have a timed version elsewhere. Music Assistant continues its search for lyrics that follow the song instead of stopping at the first block of text.
If no timed version is found, it retains the first plain version. Recently refreshed library items may take up to 90 days to be refreshed again.

pullRequests.title: Lyrics continue to search for lrc lyrics after finding plain ones

articles.title: Upload firmware without an unexpected ZIP error
articles.dek: The repair covers individual update files passed through the Z-Wave JS server.
body: A valid firmware file could fail before reaching a radio because the server tried to unpack it as an archive. Z-Wave JS continues to normal file detection when that first check fails, allowing individual GBL, HEX and OTA update files to be read.
ZIP archives remain supported, with the same file-size limits. The correction repairs file handling; the selected firmware still needs to be appropriate for the device.

pullRequests.title: fix: return `undefined` from `tryUnzipFirmwareFile` for non-ZIP data

articles.title: Old LED colour formulas need a smaller number range
articles.dek: Values above 1 become full brightness; fixed YAML percentages are unaffected.
body: Custom formulas that return red, green, blue or white values between 0 and 255 need to return a fraction between 0 and 1 instead. ESPHome removes the long-deprecated scale from light.addressable_set, so an old result such as 128 is limited to full brightness rather than interpreted as approximately half.
Dividing the existing value by 255.0 preserves its meaning. The change affects formulas written as lambdas, not fixed YAML values, which already use fractions or percentages.

pullRequests.title: [light] Remove 0-255 lambda values from addressable_set
